title: 1956 Sooners: 466 Points Scored, Only 51 Allowed
question: How many points did the 1956 Oklahoma Sooners score and allow?
answer: The 1956 Oklahoma Sooners went 10-0, outscoring opponents 466 to 51 and posting six shutouts on the way to a consensus national championship. Oklahoma played no bowl game that winter.
summary: The 1956 Oklahoma Sooners went 10-0, outscored foes 466-51 with six shutouts, won the national title and still skipped a bowl. Here is the story.
body: Bud Wilkinson's 1956 Oklahoma team is remembered as one of the most complete squads in college football history, and the season totals back that up. The Sooners finished 10-0, and a look at the final scoreboard shows 466 points for Oklahoma against just 51 for the opposition, an average of roughly 46.6 points scored and 5.1 allowed per game.

Six of those ten games were shutouts. The headline result came on October 27, 1956, when Oklahoma went to Notre Dame Stadium and won 40-0, a game that stretched the Sooners' famous winning streak and left little doubt about who the best team in the country was.

Oklahoma went 6-0 in Big Seven play that fall and finished first in both major final polls, which makes the 1956 squad a consensus national champion. It was the Sooners' third national title in seven seasons under Wilkinson, following the 1950 and 1955 teams.

The odd footnote is what happened after the regular season. The Big Seven had a rule that barred its champion from going to a bowl game in consecutive years, and Oklahoma had played in the Orange Bowl following the 1955 season. So the unbeaten national champions stayed home, while runner-up Colorado accepted the conference's bowl invitation and won the Orange Bowl.

For fans who like numbers, 466 points and 51 allowed is a handy shorthand for the peak of the Wilkinson era: a team that won every game, shut out most of its opponents more often than not, and finished on top without ever playing a postseason game.
